2.m: Of the Sāmans, [the syllables] increase by two each.
Of the Prajāpati-derived, by four each.
These are: Uṣṇih, Anuṣṭubh, Bṛhatī, Paṅkti, Triṣṭubh, and Jagatī.
By threes having the same name, taken one by one, they are Brahmā-derived.

3.m: [A metre has] one, two, three, or four quarter-verses as specified.
The first [metre, Gāyatrī, is] four-quartered with seasons [six syllables each].
Between a six-syllable and a seven-syllable [quarter-verse], one of eight [syllables makes] Atipādanicṛt.
Two nine-syllable [quarters] and one six-syllable [quarter make] Nāgī.
With six-, seven-, and eight-syllable [quarters, it is] Vardhamānā.
The third [variety of Gāyatrī has] two quarter-verses, consisting of a Jagatī-quarter and a Gāyatrī-quarter.
Uṣṇih [has] two Gāyatrī-quarters and one Jagatī-quarter.
If the last [is placed] in the middle, it is Kakubh.
Sometimes it is three-quartered with two Jagatī-quarters,

3.s: agniḥ savitā somo bṛhaspatirmitrāvaruṇāvindro viśvedevā devatāḥ
3.d: अग्निः सविता सोमो बृहस्पतिर्मित्रावरुणाविन्द्रो विश्वेदेवा देवताः

4.m: tānyabhisaṃvyāprebhyaḥ kṛtiḥ
prakṛtyā copasargavarjitaḥ
dhṛtyaṣṭiśakvarījagatyaḥ
pṛthakpiṛthakpūrvata etānyevaiṣām
atha laukikam

supratiṣṭhāpratiṣṭhāmadhyātyuktoktāśca

pādaścaturbhāgaḥ
laḥ samudrā gaṇaḥ
svarā ardhaṃ cāryārdham
atrāyuṅ na c
If nl, a word begins with the second [syllable].
A quarter-verse [ends] at three gaṇas; [this is] Pathyā, and the first [is so].
Capalā [has] the second and fourth [gaṇas] as c [i.e., amphibrachs] between heavy syllables.
Āryāgīti has eight gaṇas in a half.
Vaitālīya has twice seven morae in the odd quarter-verse, eight in the even; at the end [of each pāda are] r, l, ga.
In the remainder, an even [syllable] is not combined with the next.
[When] the preceding [syllable] is combined with the fifth, it is Prācyavṛtti.
[When combined] with the odd third, it is Udīcyavṛtti.
[When combining] both simultaneously, it is Pravṛttaka.
Ending in ga, twice eight [morae], Mātrāsamaka has the ninth [syllable] light.
And the twelfth [light is] Vānavāsikā.
Viśloka [has] the fifth and eighth [light].
Cūlikā has twenty-nine [morae in the first half] and thirty-one [in the second], ending in ga.

4.s: sā g yena na samā lāṃ gla iti
4.d: सा ग् येन न समा लां ग्ल इति
4.m: That which is not equal by ga, having l, is gla.

5.m: Isometric, semi-isometric, and heterometric.
An isometric [pattern] repeated that many times makes a semi-isometric,
Accumulated from isometric, equal, and semi-isometric,
Vaktra is an Anuṣṭubh quarter-verse.
And ra in the second and fourth [quarter-verses].
Vipulā has light and heavy, with the seventh [syllable light] in the even [quarter-verses].
Padacaturūrdhva has an increase of four [syllables] in each quarter-verse.
If two heavy syllables are at the beginning, it is Pratyāpīḍa.
By reversing the first [quarter-verse], Mañjarī, Lavalī, and Amṛtadhārā [are produced].

5.s: udgatāmekataḥ sjau slau nsau jgau bhgau jlau g sjau sjau g
5.d: उद्गतामेकतः स्जौ स्लौ न्सौ ज्गौ भ्गौ ज्लौ ग् स्जौ स्जौ ग्
5.m: Udgatā has, respectively: s and j; s, l, and [ga]; n and s; j and ga, bh and ga, j, l, and ga; s and j, s and j, and ga.
Saurabhaka has, in the third [quarter-verse], r and n, bh and ga.

5.s: upasthitapracuṣitaṃ pṛthagādyaṃ msau jbhau gau snau jrau g nau s nau n jyau
5.d: उपस्थितप्रचुषितं पृथगाद्यं म्सौ ज्भौ गौ स्नौ ज्रौ ग् नौ स् नौ न् ज्यौ
5.m: Upasthitapracuṣita has its first [quarter-verse] distinct: m and s; j and bh, and two ga's; s and n; j and r, and ga; two n's and s; two n's, j and y.
Varddhamāna has two n's; s and n; n and s.
Śuddhavirāḍṛṣabha has t, j, and r.

5.s: upacitrakaṃ sau slau g bhau bhgau g
5.d: उपचित्रकं सौ स्लौ ग् भौ भ्गौ ग्
5.m: Upacitraka has two s's, s, l, and ga; two bh's, bh and ga, and ga.

5.s: drutamadhyā bhau bhgau g njau jyau
5.d: द्रुतमध्या भौ भ्गौ ग् न्जौ ज्यौ
5.m: Drutamadhyā has two bh's, bh and ga, and ga; n and j, j and y.

5.s: vedavatī sau sgau bhau bhgau g
5.d: वेदवती सौ स्गौ भौ भ्गौ ग्
5.m: Vedavatī has two s's, s and ga; two bh's, bh and ga, and ga.

5.s: bhadravirāṭ tjau rgau msau jgau g
5.d: भद्रविराट् त्जौ र्गौ म्सौ ज्गौ ग्
5.m: Bhadravirāṭ has t and j, r and ga; m and s, j and ga, and ga.

5.s: ketumatī sjau sgau bhrau ngau g
5.d: केतुमती स्जौ स्गौ भ्रौ न्गौ ग्
5.m: Ketumatī has s and j, s and ga; bh and r, n and ga, and ga.

5.s: ākhyānakī tau jgau g jtau jgau g
5.d: आख्यानकी तौ ज्गौ ग् ज्तौ ज्गौ ग्
5.m: Ākhyānakī has two t's, j and ga, and ga; j and t, j and ga, and ga.

5.s: viparītākhyānakī jtau jgau g tau jgau g
5.d: विपरीताख्यानकी ज्तौ ज्गौ ग् तौ ज्गौ ग्
5.m: Viparītākhyānakī has j and t, j and ga, and ga; two t's, j and ga, and ga.

5.s: hariṇaplutā sau slau g nbhau bhrau
5.d: हरिणप्लुता सौ स्लौ ग् न्भौ भ्रौ
5.m: Hariṇaplutā has two s's, s, l, and ga; n and bh, bh and r.

5.s: aparavaktraṃ nau rlau g njau jrau
5.d: अपरवक्त्रं नौ र्लौ ग् न्जौ ज्रौ
5.m: Aparavaktra has two n's, r, l, and ga; n and j, j and r.

5.s: puṣpitāgrā nau ryau njau jrau g
5.d: पुष्पिताग्रा नौ र्यौ न्जौ ज्रौ ग्
5.m: Puṣpitāgrā has two n's, r and y; n and j, j and r, and ga.

5.s: yavamatī rjau rjau jrau jrau g
5.d: यवमती र्जौ र्जौ ज्रौ ज्रौ ग्
5.m: Yavamatī has r and j, r and j; j and r, j and r, and ga.
Śikhā has twenty-nine [moras] and thirty-one [moras], with a heavy syllable at the end.

6.m: Māṇavakākrīḍitaka has bh and t, l and ga.
Mayūrasāriṇī has r and j, r and ga.
Upendravajrā has j and t, j and ga, and ga.
Śālinī has m and two t's, and ga; [caesura at] the oceans (four) and the seers (seven).
Bhramaravilasita has m and bh, n, l, and ga.
Rathoddhatā has r and n, r, l, and ga.
Drutavilambita has n and bh, bh and r.
Puṭa [has] two n-gaṇas and two m-gaṇas; [the caesura is at] eight and four [syllables].
Jaloddhatagati [has] j, s, j, and s; [the caesuras are at] six and six [syllables].
Kusumavicitrā [has] n, y, n, and y.
Vaiśvadevī [has] two m-gaṇas and two y-gaṇas; [the caesuras are at] five and seven [syllables].
Vāhinī [has] t, y, m, and y; [the caesuras are at] seven and five [syllables].
Navamālinī [has] n, j, and two bh-gaṇas. Thus [ends the class of twelve-syllable metres].

7.m: Praharṣiṇī [has] m, n, j, r, and a heavy syllable; [the caesuras are at] three and ten [syllables].
Rucirā [has] j, bh, s, j, and a heavy syllable; [the caesuras are at] four and nine [syllables].
Mattamayūra [has] m, t, y, s, and a heavy syllable; [the caesuras are at] four and nine [syllables].
Asaṃbādhā [has] m, t, n, s, and two heavy syllables; [the caesuras are at] five and nine [syllables].
Aparājitā [has] two n-gaṇas, r, s, a light syllable, and a heavy syllable; [the caesuras are at] seven and seven [syllables].
Praheraṇakalitā [has] two n-gaṇas, bh, n, a light syllable, and a heavy syllable as well.
Vasantatilakā [has] t, bh, two j-gaṇas, and two heavy syllables.
[It is called] Siṃhonnatā according to Kāśyapa.
[It is called] Uddharṣiṇī according to Saitava.
Maṇiguṇanikara [has the caesuras at] eight and seven [syllables].
Ṛṣabhagajavilasita [has] bh, r, two n-gaṇas, n, and a heavy syllable; [the caesuras are at] seven and nine [syllables].
Hariṇī [has] n, s, m, r, s, a light syllable, and a heavy syllable; [the caesuras are at] six, four, and seven [syllables].

7.s: pṛthvī jsau jsau yalau g vasunavakau
7.d: पृथ्वी ज्सौ ज्सौ यलौ ग् वसुनवकौ
7.m: Pṛthvī [has] j, s, j, s, y, a light syllable, and a heavy syllable; [the caesuras are at] eight and nine [syllables].

7.s: vaṃśapatrapatitaṃ bhrau nbhau nlau g digṛṣayaḥ
7.d: वंशपत्रपतितं भ्रौ न्भौ न्लौ ग् दिगृषयः
7.m: Vaṃśapatrapatita [has] bh, r, n, bh, n, a light syllable, and a heavy syllable; [the caesuras are at] ten and seven [syllables].

7.s: mandākrāntā mbhau ntau tgau g samudrartusvarāḥ
7.d: मन्दाक्रान्ता म्भौ न्तौ त्गौ ग् समुद्रर्तुस्वराः
7.m: Mandākrāntā [has] m, bh, n, two t-gaṇas, and two heavy syllables; [the caesuras are at] four, six, and seven [syllables].
Śikhariṇī [has] y, m, n, s, bh, a light syllable, and a heavy syllable; [the caesuras are at] six and eleven [syllables].
Kusumitalatāvellitā [has] m, t, n, y, and two y-gaṇas; [the caesuras are at] five, six, and seven [syllables].
Śārdūlavikrīḍita [has] m, s, j, s, two t-gaṇas, and a heavy syllable; [the caesuras are at] twelve and seven [syllables].
Suvadanā [has] m, r, bh, n, y, bh, a light syllable, and a heavy syllable; [the caesuras are at] seven, seven, and six [syllables].

7.s: sragdharā mrau bhnau yau y triḥsaptakāḥ
7.d: स्रग्धरा म्रौ भ्नौ यौ य् त्रिःसप्तकाः
7.m: Sragdharā [has] m, r, bh, n, and three y-gaṇas; [the caesuras are] three times seven [syllables].

7.s: bhadrakaṃ bhrau nrau nrau ngau digādityāḥ
7.d: भद्रकं भ्रौ न्रौ न्रौ न्गौ दिगादित्याः
7.m: Bhadraka [has] bh, r, n, r, n, r, n, and a heavy syllable; [the caesuras are at] ten and twelve [syllables].

7.s: aśvalalitaṃ njau bhjau bhjau bhlau g rudrādityāḥ
7.d: अश्वललितं न्जौ भ्जौ भ्जौ भ्लौ ग् रुद्रादित्याः
7.m: Aśvalalita [has] n, j, bh, j, bh, j, bh, a light syllable, and a heavy syllable; [the caesuras are at] eleven and twelve [syllables].

7.s: mattākrīḍā mau tnau nau nlau g vasupañcadaśakau
7.d: मत्ताक्रीडा मौ त्नौ नौ न्लौ ग् वसुपञ्चदशकौ
7.m: Mattākrīḍā [has] two m-gaṇas, t, n, n, n, a light syllable, and a heavy syllable; [the caesuras are at] eight and fifteen [syllables].
Tanvī [has] bh, t, n, s, bh, and two y-gaṇas; [the caesuras are at] five, seven, and twelve [syllables].

7.s: krauñcapadā bhmau sbhau nau nau g bhūtendriyavasvṛṣayaḥ
7.d: क्रौञ्चपदा भ्मौ स्भौ नौ नौ ग् भूतेन्द्रियवस्वृषयः
7.m: Krauñcapadā [has] bh, m, s, bh, four n-gaṇas, and a heavy syllable; [the caesuras are at] five, five, eight, and seven [syllables].

7.s: bhucaṅgavijṛmbhitaṃ mau tnau nau rsau lgau vasurudraṛṣayaḥ
7.d: भुचङ्गविजृम्भितं मौ त्नौ नौ र्सौ ल्गौ वसुरुद्रऋषयः
7.m: Bhujaṅgavijṛmbhita [has] two m-gaṇas, t, n, n, r, s, a light syllable, and a heavy syllable; [the caesuras are at] eight, eleven, and seven [syllables].

7.s: apavāhako mnau nau nau nsau gau navarturasendriyāṇi
7.d: अपवाहको म्नौ नौ नौ न्सौ गौ नवर्तुरसेन्द्रियाणि
7.m: Apavāhaka [has] m, n, three n-gaṇas, n, s, and two heavy syllables; [the caesuras are at] nine, six, six, and five [syllables].
The first is Caṇḍavṛṣṭiprapāta [having seven r-gaṇas].
According to Rāta and Māṇḍavya, it is otherwise.

8.m: Kuḍmaladantī [has] bh, t, n, and two heavy syllables; [the caesuras are at] five and six [syllables].
Varatanu [has] n, j, j, and r; [the caesuras are at] six and six [syllables].
Jaladharamālā [has] m, bh, s, and m; [the caesuras are at] four and eight [syllables].
Lalanā [has] bh, t, n, and s; [the caesuras are at] five and seven [syllables].
Kanakaprabhā [has] s, j, s, j, and a heavy syllable.
Kuṭilagati [has] two n-gaṇas, t, and a heavy syllable; [the caesuras are at] seven and six [syllables].
Varasundarī [has] bh, j, s, n, and two heavy syllables.
Kuṭilā [has] m, bh, n, y, and a heavy syllable; [the caesuras are at] four, six, and four [syllables].
[The metre] Śailaśikhā [has the triplets] bha, ra; na, bha; bha, ga, with caesurae at five, six, and five [syllables].
Varayuvatī [has the triplets] bha, ra; ya, na; na, ga.

8.s: atiśāyinī sau jbhau jgau g diksvarāḥ
8.d: अतिशायिनी सौ ज्भौ ज्गौ ग् दिक्स्वराः
8.m: Atiśāyinī [has the triplets] sa, u [= bha]; ja, bha; ja, ga; [and a] ga, with caesurae at ten and seven [syllables].
Avitatha [has] na, ja; bha, ja; ja, la; [and a] ga.
If [the caesurae are] at eight, five, and four [syllables], it is Kokilaka.
Vibudhapriyā [has] ra, sa; ja, u [= bha]; bha, ra, with caesurae at eight and ten [syllables].

8.s: vismitā ymau nsau rau g rasartusvarāḥ
8.d: विस्मिता य्मौ न्सौ रौ ग् रसर्तुस्वराः
8.m: Vismitā [has] ya, ma; na, sa; ra, u [= bha]; ga, with caesurae at six, six, and seven [syllables].

8.s: śaśivadanā njau bhjau j jrau rudradiśaḥ
8.d: शशिवदना न्जौ भ्जौ ज् ज्रौ रुद्रदिशः
8.m: Śaśivadanā [has] na, ja; bha, ja; ja, ja, ra, with caesurae at eleven and ten [syllables].
The multiplier [two operates] in reverse order, doubling the light syllable and what follows.
When [halved] so many times, it is multiplied by that [squared].
Twice [the sum of all], minus two, of those bounded thereby.
